The new trial date was set on Monday, November 16, by a judge at Plymouth Superior Court in Massachusetts, United States. Clancy, 36, is facing three counts of first-degree murder over the January 24, 2023, deaths of her children, Cora, five; Dawson, three; and Callan, eight months. The children were found strangled at the family’s home in Duxbury, a suburb of Boston. Her first trial, which lasted several weeks, ended in a mistrial on September 4 after the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict. Eleven jurors reportedly favoured finding her not criminally responsible by reason of insanity, while one juror disagreed. Clancy’s defence team argued that she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time of the incident and should not be held criminally responsible for the children’s deaths. Her lawyers had also asked the court to dismiss the charges, arguing that another trial would violate her constitutional protection against double jeopardy. However, Judge William Sullivan rejected the application on November 9, ruling that the jury’s inability to reach a unanimous verdict provided grounds for a retrial. According to reports, prosecutors are expected to pursue another trial, although they have not formally confirmed whether they will retain the first-degree murder charges or seek lesser charges. Clancy’s lawyers have indicated that they intend to appeal the ruling permitting a retrial but said the appeal would not delay the proceedings. The former labour and delivery nurse also attempted suicide after the deaths of her children, leaving her paralysed and requiring a wheelchair. If convicted of first-degree murder, she faces a mandatory sentence of life imprisonment without the possibility of parole under Massachusetts law.
